Okay — here's the known-good state: sensor A's signal wire (yellow) goes to A0, red to 3V, black to GND, and the display should be showing a number that changes when you warm the sensor with your hand.

If that chain checks out and it still doesn't work, the fault is almost always in the rule step — the bit of the sketch that decides what number counts as "too warm." That one catches nearly everyone, so use restore and rebuild if you want a clean slate — it genuinely isn't cheating.

calls.answer:
Alright — go through the sensor test directly: warm sensor A with your fingers or breath and watch the display.

If the number on the display doesn't move at all, the break is between sensor A and A0 — check that the yellow wire is pushed firmly into A0 on the board and firmly into the signal pin on sensor A, since a loose signal wire is the single most common thing here. If the number does move, that test passes and you move to the next one: does the verdict flip when the number crosses your line?
